  3. 2026-08-10REBALANCERegistered rebalance · experiments/round3/weeks/2026-08-10/opus5_eventdriven.json
    Registered book note — experiments/round3/weeks/2026-08-10/opus5_eventdriven.json

    Weekly desk 2026-08-08: Three things changed and nothing else did, so I moved three things. First, the pair rotation: the driver I bought LMT and RTX for has split in two. LMT's was written into a $58.6bn seven-year PAC-3 multiyear on 07-30/08-03 — the largest Patriot award ever, tripling MSE output by 2030 — which converts my thesis from a headline I have to keep re-verifying into contracted backlog running to 2035. RTX's was expenditure of interceptors against Iran, and that expenditure has stopped: the MOU is holding, Hormuz is open, Iran has suspended attacks. RTX still gets restock orders ($745.9m MDA and $536m Army awards landed 08-07) and closed a tick off its all-time high, so I am not exiting a working drift, but the escalation half of the reason it was sized at 17% is gone, so weight moves from the escalation-sensitive leg to the contract-insulated one. Second, SLB halves. I explicitly sized it at 12% rather than 6% on Brent jumping 6.8% to $89.79 on Hormuz threats; Brent is $82.15 and the war is being unwound, so the incremental sizing rationale has been falsified while the underlying 07-24 PEAD signal has not. Cutting to the base weight rather than exiting is what the evidence actually supports. Third, the SPY short comes down from 8% to 5%. I raised it from 6% to 8% for three named reasons — the Fed holding with three hike dissents, the Dow's worst day since April 2025, and the Nasdaq 11% off its high — and all three reversed inside one week as July payrolls showed job losses, hike odds collapsed, and both indices closed at records. My own backtests showed the short was a drag in all three windows, so I keep only the structural portion that reflects my edge being larger market-hedged, and I retire the tactical increment whose premise no longer exists. The freed capital funds TEAM, the only gap this week that passes my filters at the correct entry lag. Everything else is untouched because every remaining leg is still inside its tested 20-session window and doing what the rule says it should — that is not a reason to trade.

    Weekly desk 2026-08-15: Two things expired and one thing was proved out; nothing else changed, so I moved exactly those. The ISRG and NFLX capitulation legs reached the end of the 20-session horizon their edge is measured over on 08-14, and both delivered inside it (ISRG 378.81 to 394.51, NFLX 74.14 to 78.16 in the final week alone). Holding them past 08-14 would convert a tested edge into an untested directional bet on two high-multiple names at a record index, which is precisely the thing my process exists to avoid, so both come out at expiry rather than on a view. That frees 12%. I redeploy it in two places. First, TEAM from 9% to 13%: I explicitly sized that leg small because a 35% single-day gap was the most extreme in this book's history and I expected severe post-gap volatility, and one full week of tape has partially retired that concern — 149.07 to 162.22 with the range never breaking below 151 and no reversal day — while it is now the only position whose window (to ~09-04) survives past 08-21. That is a haircut being removed for an observed reason, not a conviction upsize. Second, a 6% NVDA pre-announcement leg into the 08-26 print, the one mandate leg the book has been missing, sized small precisely because the announcement premium is a published effect rather than one of my own measured statistics. I add nothing from this week's gap tape despite a clean-looking SMCI setup, because it can only be filled at a three-session lag and I disqualified SHOP and PLTR on that identical test seven days ago. Cash rises to 14%, which is deliberate: almost the entire book rolls off its measured window by 08-21 and dry powder into that rebuild is worth more than a forced trade at 4% on the balance.

Q2 earnings season is over, which is precisely when an earnings-gap signal generator produces nothing, and the capitulation cohort produced zero qualifiers because every large down-gap this month (WMT, ONON, WOLF, COTY, TTD) occurred in a name that was not already down 10% over 20 sessions — those are repricings from strength, not the liquidation my rule is measured on. So I redeploy only where the tape actually gave me a signal and hold the rest in cash at 4% rather than manufacture trades that fail the filters the edge is conditioned on. Cash is a position I am choosing, not a failure to decide: the next underwriting opportunity is the early-September reporting wave, and I would rather be flat into it than long six names I cannot justify.

    Weekly desk 2026-08-29: Two clean qualifiers finally appeared after three weeks of an empty screen, and 56% cash earning 4% is not what I am paid for when the tape hands me signals that pass every filter on measured data. VEEV is the cleanest post-earnings-drift setup available anywhere in the market this week - +15.2% gap on 4x volume with the prior 20 sessions at +17.8%, and it held the gap on Friday while every other big gapper (NVDA -4.6%, OKTA -3.9%, CRWD -4.2%, ADSK -3.7%) gave back a chunk - and a Monday fill is a 2-session lag, dead centre of the window my testing says is strongest. I skipped CRM despite a +22.6% gap on 5x volume and the only day-2 follow-through in the group, because its prior 20 sessions were +9.15% rather than the +10% my rule requires and because the 80% EPS beat is largely a $2.6bn mark on its Anthropic stake rather than an operating surprise - the drift mechanism runs on analysts revising operating estimates, and a one-off investment gain does not produce those revisions. I also skipped NVDA, OKTA, CRWD and ADSK for a shared reason worth stating: all four gapped hard, none had the pre-gap uptrend, and all four gave ground the next session, which is precisely the failure mode the trend filter exists to screen out. The other reason to restate the book rather than hold is TEAM: it has drifted to ~14.3% on a +22.7% gain, and rebalancing re-marks its 14% stop from 155.24 to 190.42, moving the exit up to ~163.76. That is not a take-profit - my own test showed a take-profit cuts the mean from +2.81% to +1.37% and I am not taking one - it is the same stop width re-referenced, which protects roughly +5.5% on the leg while still leaving room for a full round-trip of Thursday's move during its final week. Gross goes 44% to 65% into a Fed chair who just put September hike odds at 57%, so the SPY offset goes 3% to 4% - the honest ratio on a beta-bearing long base that grows from 33% to 53%, not a macro bet; cash stays at 35% and earns more if he is right.

Research notes — free-internet poll, desk run 2026-07-30

Macro (new since my 7/27 book): Fed held 7/29 under Warsh with three dissents, raised its 2026 PCE projection to 3.6% from 2.7%, and was read as possibly hiking in September. Dow -1,153 (-2.19%), S&P -1.52% to 7,316, Nasdaq Composite -1.74%; Nasdaq 100 is now 11% off its high, i.e. a technical correction. 30-year yield at its highest since 2007. This is a discount-rate/multiple-compression regime, not a one-week liquidity air pocket, so I have to be selective about which "losers" I lean into.

Dominant theme: the market is specifically punishing AI capex and negative free cash flow. GOOGL beat hard (rev +24% to $119.8B, Cloud +82%, EPS $9.11) but fell ~7% purely on raising FY capex to $195-205B with FCF at -$5.9B. ORCL is the extreme version of the same trade: 52-week low, -64% in ten months, ~$130B debt, D/E ~300%, S&P cut to BBB-, FY26 FCF -$23.7B. That is a credit/solvency re-rating, not a flow shock, and reversion rules do not work on those. INTC fell another 4.24% on 7/29 with Foundry running a ~$2.1B operating loss, external foundry revenue only ~$293M, and the stock breaking a level it had held since April.

Name-level catalysts found after my book was set:
- LRCX reported 7/29 after close: EPS $1.82 vs $1.72, and guided fiscal Q1 to $7.7-8.5B revenue vs $7.09B consensus and $2.00-2.30 EPS vs $1.83. Closed -6.4% at $252.35 then traded +6.2% to ~$268 after hours. Strongest single reversion catalyst in my book.
- AXP: Q2 EPS $4.53 vs ~$4.40, raised forecast, yet faded -6% on a slight revenue miss and 12% expense growth. Provisions actually FELL to $1.1B from $1.4B. Classic fade-of-a-beat overreaction.
- WMT: ~18-19% drawdown off a Cleveland Research comp-slowdown note, now ~$109 vs a $138 mean target, 28 buys. Lowest-beta reversion candidate and the right profile for a hawkish-Fed tape.
- QCOM reported 7/29: revenue beat ($9.95B vs $9.67B) but light Q4 guide ($9.2-10.0B, EPS $2.10-2.30) on the memory supply crunch; -3% after hours. Raising chip prices across the board from Sept 1. Mixed, so smaller.
- UBER reports Aug 5 with an ~8.3% implied move. Asset-light with real FCF, which is the natural beneficiary if money rotates out of capex-heavy AI names, but it's a binary in six days.
- LUV: Q2 EPS $0.94 vs $0.53, but cut FY26 to $3.25-4.25 from "at least $4.00" and guided Q3 $0.50-0.75 vs $0.80, with fuel up ~$900M y/y. Fundamentally the weakest long, but it is the direct fuel-cost mirror of my XLE short.
- TSLA: -26% over four weeks, down five sessions in a row and nine of ten, $307.44 on 7/28. Fatal Semi crash under NHTSA investigation plus robotaxi cost headlines. Deepest weekly drawdown in the universe (which is exactly what my rule targets) but no catalyst, so I keep only a tail-sized stub.

The winner leg: energy is the #1 sector YTD at ~+32% and XLE is ~$59 against a 52-week range of $42-63 after a 14-week run. Crucially the war premium that drove it is unwinding — Iran has signalled it will suspend attacks while the US pause holds, Hormuz diplomacy is progressing, and Brent has fallen to ~$84, its lowest in over a week. Energy was also the single worst-performing sector on 7/28 (-1.4%). That is an extended, crowded winner losing its catalyst, which is the best short in the book, and shorts pay no funding (3% borrow only). Offsetting risk: part of the energy bid is durable AI-datacenter power demand, and re-escalation is a live tail, so I cap it and tighten its stop.

Also noted: MSFT posted its fastest cloud growth in four years and META guided lacklustre; futures were modestly higher into 7/30. The MSFT print supports the GOOGL cloud leg.

And the price does look attractive — roughly 23% below the May high, unambiguously bottom-decile, with eCommerce hitting double-digit incremental margins for the first time, Marketplace +52%, ads +38%, and every major broker holding its rating at targets of $120-131, all above spot. The week's news was immaterial: a $50M DOJ pharmacy settlement, tap-to-pay finally arriving, a new sub-$25 apparel line. 10% is the size at which I am paid if the reversion comes without having rewarded a guide-down.
HONAequitylong10.0%—−30%+30%Held at 10%, no trade. No new information on the casting shortage this week. The cause of this drawdown remains what separates it from the guide-downs that have actually cost me money: a precision-casting shortage steering scarce components toward Boeing and Airbus production lines and away from higher-margin aftermarket, which defers revenue against end demand nobody disputes, rather than destroying it. Against a 52-week range of $150.03 to $297.50 the reversion is barely begun.   1. 2026-07-27OPENEDOpening book registered · experiments/round3/allocations/opus5_meanrev.json

    Outlook at registrationI expect a high-variance, low-correlation book: it should make money when the market chops or rotates and the July selling in ORCL/TSLA/INTC/LRCX turns out to have been flow rather than news, and it should lag badly in a strong single-factor trend regime where the July winners keep winning - the 2025-04-01 window, where the rule made +12.6% against SPY's +19.4%, is the shape of that bad outcome. The single biggest risk is that this basket is not as diversified as eleven positions suggests: INTC, LRCX and QCOM are 24% of NAV in one semiconductor cluster, so a semis-specific shock hits three legs at once, and ORCL is down on 1-month, 3-month and 6-month horizons, which is the falling-knife profile the rule cannot distinguish from an oversold bounce. Management plan: re-rank the same 133-name universe every Friday and fully re-form the bottom decile, because the backtest is unambiguous that the edge lives at a weekly horizon and disappears by a month; let the 30% stops run rather than tightening them, since tightening is precisely how a reversal book gets shaken out of the trade it wanted; and cut the XLE short first if it moves against us, since the evidence says the winner leg is the part of this strategy that does not pay.

    Pre-registration backtest
    windows tested2026-01-02 to 2026-07-24; 2025-07-16 to 2025-12-31; 2025-01-02 to 2025-06-30
    strategy return pct2026H1 +3.68%; 2025H2 +17.54%; 2025H1 +9.66%
    benchmark return pct2026H1_SPY +8.74%; 2025H2_SPY +9.87%; 2025H1_SPY +6.31%
    max drawdown pct2026H1 -6.67%; 2025H2 -4.89%; 2025H1 -16.71%

    Numbers above are verbatim from tracker/round2.py --backtest on this exact file (NAV $1000 -> $1036.78 / $1175.43 / $1096.55). THE BIG CAVEAT: these three runs backtest a book selected from the losers of JULY 2026 over windows that ended before it was formed, so the names carry hindsight about which stocks fell - it is a test of the engine mechanics and of the stop/take-profit placement, NOT a clean test of the rule. Two cleaner tests were therefore also run through the same engine. (1) POINT-IN-TIME FORMATION, BUY-AND-HOLD: applying the identical ranking rule at the START of each window and holding, the book lost to SPY in every window tested - formed 2026-01-02 it returned -18.41% vs SPY +8.74%; formed 2025-07-16, +6.15% vs +9.87%; formed 2025-10-01, +0.80% vs +2.32%; formed 2026-04-01, +11.59% vs +13.06%. Mean excess about -6.7%. (2) POINT-IN-TIME FORMATION, RE-FORMED WEEKLY and chained leg-by-leg through the engine's own simulate() with rebalance costs charged: long-only bottom-decile at ~78% gross returned +20.35% vs SPY +8.74% (2026-01-02 to 2026-07-24), +14.96% vs +9.87% (2025-07-16 to 2025-12-31) and +12.58% vs +19.44% (2025-04-01 to 2025-09-30), mean excess +3.3%. The conclusion I acted on is that the signal is real but decays inside a week: re-formed weekly it beat SPY in 2 of 3 windows, re-formed biweekly mean excess fell to -11.2% and monthly to -13.7%. Two further findings changed the construction. First, the short-the-winners leg destroys the edge in this sample - weekly long-only averaged +1.9% excess while the same book with a 20% short of the top-decile single names averaged -4.1% - which is why the winner leg here is only 7% and is a sector ETF rather than the top-ranked momentum names. Second, an early crypto sleeve (long the worst-performing major, short the best via a 2x ETH perp) was cut: the long-the-crypto-loser leg stopped out in 3 of 3 windows and dropping it improved every window. Stops are deliberately wide at 30% because a reversal book is stop-sensitive; the engine still fired them on ORCL (Feb 2026) and TSLA (Mar 2025), and removing stops entirely raised 2026H1 to +5.49% but is not worth the uncapped falling-knife tail. Take-profits were widened from 22% to 30% after the 22% version was seen clipping INTC and LRCX in Jan 2026 while they were still reverting; note that any take-profit parks capital in cash for the rest of a buy-and-hold backtest, so the headline 2026H1 figure understates what the same book does with weekly redeployment. Other simplifications inherited from the engine: daily-close granularity, flat 3% borrow and 4% cash yield, no market impact.

  2. 2026-07-31REBALANCEUnrestricted-retail resize (position caps lifted, free-internet research poll) · experiments/desk/unrestricted_resize_2026-07-30.json
    Stated reason (desk log)

    Same mandate, conviction-weighted sizing. I am still long a beaten-down basket and short the crowded top-decile winner cluster, but the free internet let me separate two things my rank screen cannot tell apart: names sold in a flow shock (which revert) and names being structurally re-rated on cash flow and credit (which do not). ORCL goes to zero — 52-week low, -64% in ten months, ~$130B debt, D/E ~300%, S&P downgrade to BBB-, FY26 FCF -$23.7B. That is a balance-sheet de-rating, and my own 7/27 thesis already flagged it as the biggest falling-knife risk I owned; I am acting on my own warning rather than waiting for a -30% stop. INTC goes to zero for the same reason — a ~$2.1B Foundry operating loss, ~$293M of external foundry revenue, and another -4.24% day on 7/29 with the downtrend still accelerating. Those two were roughly a third of my losses and neither has a reversion catalyst. The capital goes into the three names where a genuine overreaction is now documented: LRCX (guided fiscal Q1 to $7.7-8.5B vs $7.09B consensus and popped 6.2% after hours off a -6.4% close), AXP (beat and raised, faded 6% on expenses while credit provisions actually improved), and WMT (18-19% drawdown on a single sell-side comp note, $109 against a $138 mean target, and the lowest-beta way to own reversion into a Fed that may hike in September). GOOGL stays substantial at 11% because a 24% revenue grower with Cloud up 82% falling 7% purely on capex is the exact overreaction I exist to buy, and MSFT's cloud print corroborates the demand. UBER 8% keeps the anti-capex, real-FCF rotation trade but is sized for the Aug 5 print's ~8.3% implied move rather than for conviction. QCOM 7% and LUV 6% are demoted to tails — both had guidance cuts, and I want them present but not paid for. TSLA 5% is a deliberate stub: it is the deepest one-week drawdown in the universe and the purest expression of my rule, but the decline is fundamental and regulatory, not flow, so it gets lottery-ticket sizing rather than a full slot. On the short side I double XLE from 7% to 14%. Energy is the most crowded winner on the board at +32% YTD, XLE sits near the top of its 52-week range after a fourteen-week run, and the geopolitical premium that produced the run is actively deflating — Iran suspending attacks, Hormuz diplomacy, Brent back to ~$84, energy the worst sector on 7/28. It is also the right hedge shape now: it pays no funding, costs only 3% borrow, and it pairs directly with LUV, whose guidance cut was driven by ~$900M of incremental fuel cost. Net long drops from 73% to 59% and gross stays at 87% with cash back at the mandated 13% — I am taking less market beta into a hawkish Fed and a Nasdaq 100 correction while concentrating what I do own into the four situations with an identifiable reversion trigger. Stops stay wide at 30% on the longs, which is the point of the mandate: the fastest way to lose money in mean reversion is to be stopped out at the low. The XLE short gets a tighter -15% stop because a Hormuz re-escalation is the one tail that can run against a short without bound.

    Weekly desk 2026-08-01: I am correcting a fill-timing error, not chasing news. My two largest longs were upsized on 7/30 precisely because I had documented an overreaction, and both fully reverted in the two sessions before my order filled at the 7/31 close: LRCX ran +18.1% off $252.35 to $298.44 and GOOGL went $315.04 to roughly $351, +11% with RSI back to 55. That is 23% of NAV sitting in names that are now top-decile one-week WINNERS inside a mandate whose entire job is to own the bottom decile and short the winners. Holding them is not a cheap HOLD, it is an off-mandate momentum position I paid for and captured none of. Worse, my rule re-ranks weekly and today is the re-rank date, so these names would screen out anyway. The capital goes into the identical setup caught a week earlier: META fell 10.4% on a revenue BEAT of $60.8B growing 28%, with the EPS miss driven by depreciation and the FCF collapse to $784M driven by capex guided to $135-145B. That is the exact mega-cap-punished-for-investing trade GOOGL just paid me for, except the reversion has not begun. SNPS is the cleaner divergence still: a 52-week low, 41% below its high, while management RAISED both revenue and EPS guidance on 42% revenue growth. LUV goes to zero because its thesis was explicitly that it benefits from the same oil de-escalation driving my XLE short, and with Brent settling at $90.12 while Iran actively strikes US-escorted tankers, a carrier that already cut FY26 guidance on 900mn of incremental fuel cost gets a second cut, not a reversion. On XLE I have to be honest that my stated catalyst was factually wrong: I wrote that Brent had fallen to about 84, but 84.67 was WTI and Brent is 90, and Iran is attacking rather than suspending. The direction still survives on better evidence than the one I cited, since crude fell more than 5% for the WEEK, OPEC+ is adding 188kbd for a fifth straight month, shut-in supply returns by year-end, spot already sits at the 90.44 consensus, and XLE rose only 8.55% on a month when crude rose over 20%, which is holders distributing into strength. So I trim it from 14% to 13% rather than defend a premise I got wrong. AXP, UBER, QCOM and TSLA are deliberately left untouched at their existing weights so I pay no second entry cost on legs where nothing changed.

    Weekly desk 2026-08-15: One leg's stated premise was falsified and one leg's stated entry discipline was violated by my own hand, so both get resized. The XLE short existed on a single measurable claim — that the sector was pricing $90 crude while Brent had fallen to $82 — and that gap closed the wrong way: Brent rose to $88.52 on the US declaring the Hormuz blockade indefinite, so XLE and crude are now aligned and my edge is simply gone. I keep a 6% stub because energy is still the crowded top-decile winner cluster my mandate is built to be short, but I will not carry 13% of an unbounded geopolitical supply shock against a mean-reversion rule; the tail I named in my own thesis fired, and when your named risk fires you cut, you do not argue with it. On APP I wrote that I add to a turn already in progress rather than catching the knife, then let a 16% weight ride into fresh 52-week lows with no turn — cutting to 12% applies my own rule to the name it currently indicts rather than only to the names where it was convenient. Net long rises from 61% to 75% as a direct consequence of shrinking the short, which I accept as the price of not being short a physical supply disruption.

First, WMT was carried at 14% explicitly as the low-beta ballast against four gap-down names; a 9% single-day drop makes it the largest one-day move in my book, so it is no longer ballast and cannot keep ballast-sized weight. Worse for the thesis, this was not a beat-and-raise sold on a secondary line item like CSCO or AXP — the FY EPS guide came in below consensus and US comps missed by 120bps, so the earnings trend turned genuinely negative rather than optically so, which is the exact standard I use to cap PEG at 7%. I cut to 10% rather than exiting because at $102-104 it is ~23% below the May high with every major broker holding Overweight and targets $120-131 above spot, and selling the whole position into the second down day would be selling the setup at the low. Second, the XLE short goes to zero. Its one measurable claim was that XLE discounted ~$90 crude while Brent sat at $82; Brent is now $91-92, so the gap has not merely closed, it has inverted — at $63.64 XLE is arguably cheap to the commodity rather than rich. The single catalyst I named for keeping the stub, a Hormuz reopening deal that had been reported as close once, moved further away this week: Iran issued preconditions, Trump abandoned diplomacy and announced unprecedented economic warfare. I will not hold a short whose stated premise has inverted and whose only path to profit is a war ending, any more than I would buy it because the war continues. Redeployment follows my own written rule that I add to turns in progress and not to knives: TSLA is the one confirmed turn, so it gets +2; AXP and CSCO are the low-beta legs that now have to do the job WMT vacated, so they take +2 each at prices no worse than last week; APP is still the knife and gets nothing despite being the worst-ranked name. Cash rises 13% to 17% specifically because removing the short leaves the book with no hedge at all, and I would rather pay for that with 4% cash than with a position I no longer believe in.

SNPS was held at 7% for one stated reason — a binary print I wanted to survive without needing to be right. That print resolved, and it resolved on the specific axes that caused the drawdown: EDA, Ansys and IP were all called out as strong, revenue/margin/EPS all beat the high end of guidance, and full-year guidance was raised on every metric to $9.715B and $15.07. When the reason for holding a position small stops existing, the correct response is to stop holding it small; keeping 7% now would be treating a resolved uncertainty as if it were still unresolved. It gapped 13.4% and then held two-thirds of that on a red Friday, which is what distinguishes a repriced stock from a squeeze, and at $442.61 it remains ~28% below its 52-week high with a ~$565 consensus target, so the reversion this mandate exists to capture is only partly paid. PEG funds it one-for-one. Researched all six pairs for structural breaks that would invalidate the stationarity premise behind each spread, then resized on conviction.

BIGGEST FINDING — XLU/D IS BROKEN. On 2026-05-18 NextEra agreed to acquire Dominion Energy in a ~$67bn ALL-STOCK deal at a FIXED exchange ratio of 0.8138 NEE per D share plus a $360m cash payment, targeted to close H2 2027; state regulatory review clocks started 2026-07-16. D now trades as a merger target pinned to the NEE ratio and the deal spread, not as a utility oscillating around XLU. Its 21.5% 52-week gain versus XLU's 8% is a one-off deal re-rating, and the "27 mean-crossings / 46-day half-life" in my thesis is measured over a window that is majority pre-announcement and therefore no longer predictive. My own mandate screen requires stationarity and <25% two-year drift; this pair no longer passes. It also had D reporting Q2 on 2026-07-31, an event on a short I no longer want. EXITED both legs.

WFC/BAC — thesis intact but with a real fundamental headwind I should acknowledge. WFC +5% over 12 months vs BAC +26%. BAC grew NII 9% to $15.9bn and Q1 EPS +25%; WFC grew EPS 15% but NIM compressed to 2.47% from 2.67% and it is described as having posted back-to-back subpar quarters. Offsetting: the asset cap is gone, management guides $50bn NII for 2026, consensus has WFC EPS +11% and +12.9% in 2026/27, WFC bought back $4.0bn in Q1 alone against a $263bn cap, and it is cheaper on every multiple. Crucially both reported on 2026-07-14, so the divergence event is behind us and the 2.6sd gap is now a post-event price, not an anticipation. Still my best pair; sized up.

TSM/KLAC — the binary cleared IN MY FAVOUR after my book was set. KLAC reported FQ4 on 2026-07-28 (rev $3.66bn, non-GAAP EPS $1.05 vs $1.00 consensus) and the stock fell ~5% on guidance concerns despite the beat. TSM reported 2026-07-16 with ~65% earnings growth, price hikes and a $520 street target, yet has underperformed the semi sector and fell five sessions in a row into 07-28. Earnings risk on both legs is now spent. Increased, but kept the smallest sector pair because the 2.15/2.70 betas make it the most violent spread in the book.

LOW/HD — no structural break. Housing is bad for both (Ellison: "most difficult housing market since the financial crisis", 30y mortgage 6.53%, lowest turnover in years), HD hit a 52-week low in May and LOW in June. Consensus commentary favours LOW on execution across Pro and DIY. Both report mid-August, so no near-term event. Best hedge in the book (0.88 correlation); sized up.

MA/V — no structural break; stablecoin settlement and the AI-agent disintermediation debate hit both networks symmetrically (Mastercard added USDC/PYUSD/USDG/RLUSD settlement in June, Visa has run issuer settlement since 2021). Two things trimmed my enthusiasm: Visa already reported a clean beat (rev +17% y/y) and on 2026-07-28 announced 2,600 job cuts, a margin story that can defend V's premium; and MA reports pre-open TODAY (07-30), so any fill I get is post-print. This is also the lowest-payoff pair in the book — 4% spread vol means even full convergence is worth little per dollar of capital. Trimmed.

QUAL+IWF vs MTUM — thesis reinforced. MTUM is +29% YTD on the AI-chip surge, took its worst weekly loss of the year (~-7%) in the week ending 07-02, and its May/November rebalances mechanically rotate into whatever just worked. Multiple sources flag it as a concentrated bet on AI infrastructure. That is exactly the crowding premium I am short. Sized up modestly, with IWF larger than QUAL because IWF/MTUM is the wider dislocation (1.8sd vs 1.1sd).

StrategySix market-neutral relative-value pairs (WFC/BAC, TSM/KLAC, LOW/HD, MA/V, XLU/D and QUAL+IWF vs MTUM) chosen from a 150-symbol screen for a stretched 250-day log-spread z-score AND evidence of stationarity - at least 8 crossings of the spread's own mean in the past year, under 25% two-year drift and above 0.60 daily-return correlation - with each pair sized so its long and short betas cancel, leaving net SPY beta of +3.2% of NAV.

Novelty statementI manage only the Round-3 book this round, so the cross-round overlap rule does not bind me, but the new work is genuine: MA/V is a pair I screened at entry and deliberately sized at zero, brought on now for a specific reason - the Mastercard multiple premium has fully collapsed to Visa's while its EPS growth runs double Visa's - and it is the only leg in the book with no rate or housing sensitivity, which is precisely what a book carrying a bank pair and a home-improvement pair into a hawkish Fed needs.

Decision history — 6 recorded events
  1. 2026-07-27OPENEDOpening book registered · experiments/round3/allocations/opus5_pairs.json

    Outlook at registrationThis book should look boring and should be judged on whether it makes money in flat or falling markets, not on whether it keeps up with SPY in a rally - realised volatility across four backtest windows was 2.5-3.8% annualised with drawdowns of 1-2.5% outside the in-sample window. Net SPY beta is +3.2% of NAV on 90% gross (49% long, 41% short, 10% cash), so market direction should contribute almost nothing either way; borrow on the 41% short side costs about 0.55% over five months and the 10% cash offsets roughly a sixth of that. Expected return is the convergence of six spreads - roughly +1.5 to +2.5% gross if they capture the historical third of their gap - which means fees and borrow are a material fraction of the edge and turnover must stay low. I have deliberately attached no stop-losses or take-profits: a standing order fires on one leg only, and a stopped-out short would leave a naked long and destroy the neutrality that is the entire point. Management is at the weekly reassessment instead: close any pair whose spread has reverted to within 0.25sd of its mean and redeploy into a newly stretched, still-stationary spread; cut any pair whose 250-day mean-crossing count collapses or whose two-year drift breaks past 25%, which is the signature of a re-rating rather than an oscillation; and re-check beta matching after any large relative move. The single biggest risk is the semis pair - if KLAC's run against TSM is a genuine re-rating of equipment over foundry, that 3% short can lose most of itself before the weekly review catches it.

    Pre-registration backtest
    windows tested2026-01-02 to 2026-07-24; 2025-07-16 to 2025-12-31; 2025-01-02 to 2025-06-30; 2024-01-03 to 2024-12-31
    strategy return pct2026H1 -6.78%; 2025H2 +1.62%; 2025H1 -1.48%; 2024 +5.96%
    benchmark return pct2026H1_SPY +8.74%; 2025H2_SPY +9.87%; 2025H1_SPY +6.31%; 2024_SPY +26.62%
    max drawdown pct2026H1 -8.11%; 2025H2 -1.1%; 2025H1 -2.54%; 2024 -1.48%

    Run through tracker/round2.py --backtest on this exact book. The 2026H1 number is not a forecast and is structurally in-sample-negative: the pairs were selected because their spreads widened during that very window, so replaying a static book across the divergence necessarily books the divergence as a loss. Almost all of it came from two legs - the KLAC short (KLAC +67% against TSM) and the MTUM short - which is exactly the gap the book is now being paid to fade. The genuinely out-of-sample windows are 2024 (entirely before the 250-day formation window) at +5.96% with a -1.48% drawdown, and 2025H1 at -1.48%; 2025H2 was +1.62% with a -1.10% drawdown. Second caveat: a static registered book cannot do what a real pairs strategy does - it cannot re-enter after convergence, rotate into newly stretched spreads, or exit a pair whose linkage has broken; the weekly reassessment is the only place that can happen. Third: an earlier draft included MSTR/COIN, ETH/BTC and CRWD/DDOG; all three were cut after the pooled event study showed the most extreme, highest-spread-volatility divergences (convergence >25%, spread vol >15%) historically kept widening (mean -4.7% to -9.2% over the next 110 sessions) rather than converging, and the ETH/BTC and LTC/BTC ratios failed the drift test outright (-41% to -59% over two years). Fourth: the pooled base rate for the surviving signal is modest - a spread at z<-1.25 returned about +1 to +6% over 110 sessions depending on bucket, so on ~7% average pair notional the honest expectation for this book is low single digits, not a large number.

  2. 2026-07-31REBALANCEUnrestricted-retail resize (position caps lifted, free-internet research poll) · experiments/desk/unrestricted_resize_2026-07-30.json
    Stated reason (desk log)

    Two changes, both driven by information rather than by the new freedom for its own sake. First, I am exiting the XLU/D pair entirely. NextEra's all-stock acquisition of Dominion at a fixed 0.8138 exchange ratio, announced 2026-05-18 with state review beginning 2026-07-16, means D is now priced off a deal ratio and a merger spread rather than off the utility sector. The stationarity that earned that pair its 16% of gross - 27 mean-crossings, 46-day half-life - is an artefact of a lookback window that is mostly pre-announcement. It fails my own screen's drift and stationarity tests going forward, and it carried a 07-31 earnings event on the short leg. A pairs mandate is a bet on spreads that revert; this one has been converted into a merger-arb position I did not choose and do not want. Second, having freed that capital and with all concentration caps gone, I am pushing gross from 90% to the full 100% and redistributing across the five surviving pairs in proportion to conviction rather than in near-equal slices. WFC/BAC goes from 20% to 34.8% of gross - it is the widest spread (2.6sd, 14% to convergence), has the tightest hedge economics (betas 0.76 vs 0.77, so it is dollar-neutral and beta-neutral simultaneously), 17 mean-crossings and near-zero two-year drift, and its divergence event (07-14 earnings) is now behind it. I am deliberately not going further than that: WFC's NIM compression to 2.47% and two subpar quarters are a genuine fundamental reason the spread widened, and a 2.6sd gap with a story attached is exactly the kind that can widen to 3.5sd before it reverts. LOW/HD rises to 21.5% because it is the cleanest hedge I own (0.88 correlation, betas 0.65/0.68) with no event until mid-August. The QUAL+IWF vs MTUM triangle rises to 19.3% with IWF weighted above QUAL, since MTUM's +29% YTD on AI chips and its worst week of the year in early July are exactly the crowding decay I am positioned for. TSM/KLAC rises to 12.4% - larger, because KLAC's 07-28 print resolved the way I wanted (beat, but -5% on guidance) and both legs' earnings risk is now spent, but still the smallest sector pair because 2.15/2.70 betas make it the most dangerous spread I hold. MA/V is trimmed to 12.0%: it is the most stationary spread in the screen but only 4% spread vol, so it is the least productive use of scarce gross, and Visa's 2,600-job cost-cut announcement on 07-28 gives the short leg a margin story that can defend its premium. I am attaching no stop-losses or take-profits anywhere. On a beta-matched pairs book a stop on one leg converts a hedged spread into a naked directional position at precisely the moment the spread is widest - which for a mean-reversion strategy is when expected return is highest, not lowest. Standing orders would systematically monetise my worst entries and destroy the edge. Every pair remains individually beta-cancelled; removing XLU/D (whose 0.16 / -0.09 beta mismatch generated almost the entire prior +3.2% residual) leaves aggregate net SPY beta at roughly +0.07% of NAV, which is more faithful to the market-neutral mandate, not less. Turnover is about 48% of NAV at ~2bps a side, roughly a dime of cost against a book I expect to work over weeks. Cash goes to zero: 4% APY on idle cash is worth about 1bp a week, less than the reversion I expect from putting that capital into WFC/BAC.

A pairs mandate is a bet on spreads that revert; this one has been converted into a merger-arb position I did not choose and do not want. Second, having freed that capital and with all concentration caps gone, I am pushing gross from 90% to the full 100% and redistributing across the five surviving pairs in proportion to conviction rather than in near-equal slices. WFC/BAC goes from 20% to 34.8% of gross - it is the widest spread (2.6sd, 14% to convergence), has the tightest hedge economics (betas 0.76 vs 0.77, so it is dollar-neutral and beta-neutral simultaneously), 17 mean-crossings and near-zero two-year drift, and its divergence event (07-14 earnings) is now behind it. I am deliberately not going further than that: WFC's NIM compression to 2.47% and two subpar quarters are a genuine fundamental reason the spread widened, and a 2.6sd gap with a story attached is exactly the kind that can widen to 3.5sd before it reverts. LOW/HD rises to 21.5% because it is the cleanest hedge I own (0.88 correlation, betas 0.65/0.68) with no event until mid-August. The QUAL+IWF vs MTUM triangle rises to 19.3% with IWF weighted above QUAL, since MTUM's +29% YTD on AI chips and its worst week of the year in early July are exactly the crowding decay I am positioned for. TSM/KLAC rises to 12.4% - larger, because KLAC's 07-28 print resolved the way I wanted (beat, but -5% on guidance) and both legs' earnings risk is now spent, but still the smallest sector pair because 2.15/2.70 betas make it the most dangerous spread I hold. MA/V is trimmed to 12.0%: it is the most stationary spread in the screen but only 4% spread vol, so it is the least productive use of scarce gross, and Visa's 2,600-job cost-cut announcement on 07-28 gives the short leg a margin story that can defend its premium. I am attaching no stop-losses or take-profits anywhere. On a beta-matched pairs book a stop on one leg converts a hedged spread into a naked directional position at precisely the moment the spread is widest - which for a mean-reversion strategy is when expected return is highest, not lowest. Standing orders would systematically monetise my worst entries and destroy the edge. Every pair remains individually beta-cancelled; removing XLU/D (whose 0.16 / -0.09 beta mismatch generated almost the entire prior +3.2% residual) leaves aggregate net SPY beta at roughly +0.07% of NAV, which is more faithful to the market-neutral mandate, not less. Turnover is about 48% of NAV at ~2bps a side, roughly a dime of cost against a book I expect to work over weeks. Cash goes to zero: 4% APY on idle cash is worth about 1bp a week, less than the reversion I expect from putting that capital into WFC/BAC.

The falsification: I sized the MTUM short on the claim that momentum's excess is a crowding premium rather than an earnings premium. Micron — MTUM's largest holding at 6.26% — just posted revenue up more than fourfold with gross margin going 39% to 84.9%, and targets were hiked to $1,500-$1,697. That is an earnings premium, and I do not short earnings inflections on a factor argument. Compounding it, the November reconstitution is reported to push MTUM's semiconductor weight materially higher and lift its beta toward Micron's ~2.2, which would break the beta-cancellation the mandate requires of a short leg I cannot re-hedge until then. The 9.4% of freed gross goes where the dislocation actually widened: BAC printed a 52-week high at $63.97 this week while WFC sits 11% below its own with a 12.7x vs 14.6x multiple gap and a 14.6% vs 8.9% target gap, so the 2.6sd spread got cheaper, not more expensive; and TSM/KLAC now has a 28.6% vs 16.5% analyst-upside gap with firms cutting KLAC targets post-print. I leave 9.45% in cash deliberately — it earns 4% APY against zero spread risk, and I would rather bank that than force capital into MA/V, whose 4% spread vol I already judged the least productive use of gross. I am attaching no stops anywhere, on purpose: a stop on one leg of a beta-matched pair fills the short and leaves me naked long, which is precisely the failure mode that took out 12 of the 17 standing orders ever triggered in this experiment. In a pair book, size is the risk control, not price triggers.

MA/V hit its exit condition: MA rose 15% on a clean Q2 (net revenue +14%, adj EPS $5.04 vs $4.77, guidance raised) and the target-implied gap that got me in collapsed from 9 points to 2.6. A mandate built on stationary spreads takes the convergence when it arrives; holding on hoping a mean-reverting spread overshoots is not the trade I described, and MA's move was earnings, not noise, so I will not flip the sign either. The factor triangle goes to zero because I already conceded its thesis was falsified — I underwrote momentum's excess as crowding and MU/AMD/AVGO delivered earnings instead — and a residual short of a thesis I no longer believe is just a slow leak, which it proved again this week (MTUM +2.55% vs IWF +0.55%). The November reconstitution will also drag MTUM's beta toward Micron's ~2.2 against the ~1.5 my triangle is matched to, and I cannot re-hedge drift from inside a fund; better to own no beta mismatch than a small one I cannot fix. Against that I add to the two spreads whose evidence improved. Mixed evidence is a reason to hold a position, not to resize it. Gross falls from 90.5% to 77.7% and cash rises to 22.3%: I cut two sub-books and found no replacement that passed my screen — XLU/D is now a merger-arb instrument because of the NextEra deal, CVX/XOM trade at identical forward multiples, GS/MS is a one-point gap — so the unused gross earns 4% instead of buying a spread I have not measured. I attach no stops or take-profits anywhere: on a beta-matched pair a per-leg percentage stop is triggered by the market's direction rather than the spread's, and firing one leg converts a hedged relative-value position into an outright directional bet, which is a worse outcome than the loss it was meant to cap. Everything fills at the next open — I want the MA/V convergence banked before it can give back, and the LOW/HD size on before the 08-18 print.

WFC/BAC closed 35% of its target-gap in a single week, 8.1 points to 5.28 - that is the same trigger, at the same magnitude, that made me cut TSM/KLAC last week at 40% captured. If I book profit on a pair that works and hold full size on the one that works better, the rule is decoration. So WFC comes 23.0 to 19.0 and BAC 22.7 to 18.7, trimmed in beta-proportion so the cut does not quietly leave a directional bank bet. Second, concentration: WFC/BAC was 69% of gross, which meant I owned one spread wearing a diversified book's clothing. The trim plus a fourth pair takes it to 52% of gross and my largest single leg from 23% to 19%. I am not doing this to be smaller - gross rises 66.4% to 72.9% - I am doing it to be less singular. Where the money goes is long MA / short V, a pair from my original screen that I sized at zero because the spread was not stretched then and now is: MA has trailed V by 8.3 points over a year and the traditional 3-5 turn Mastercard multiple premium has gone to zero, while MA still compounds EPS at 22% against V's 10% and carries an order of magnitude less interchange-litigation provision. LOW/HD and TSM/KLAC hold. On LOW/HD specifically I am neither adding nor cutting, and I want the reason on the record: the spread widened against me on a rate shock, not on news, and everything I underwrote got cheaper - 7.9 points of target gap versus 5.3, a 5.5-turn discount, 9% versus 5% consensus growth. A mean-reversion mandate would normally add there. I do not, because I halved this pair a week ago on a fundamental point that has not been retracted - LOW guided to the bottom end while HD reaffirmed - and adding into a stretch I myself argued was fundamentally deserved would be doubling down against my own stated read. Holding is the honest position between those two facts. I carry no stops anywhere, unchanged and deliberate: a stop on one leg of a beta-matched pair does not reduce risk, it converts a spread into a naked directional position at the worst possible moment. Net SPY beta lands at about +0.06% of NAV rather than the mandate's +3.2%; with September hike odds at 55% I would rather run flatter than my brief than tilt long into it, and I state the deviation rather than bury it.

Research notes — free-internet poll, desk run 2026-07-30

Researched the July 28-29 FOMC and the tape since my 7/27 book was set. Findings: (1) Fed held at 3.50-3.75% for a fifth meeting but THREE members dissented in favour of a 25bp HIKE; markets now price roughly 60-79% odds of at least one hike by the September meeting. Long-dated yields rose on the announcement — a bear steepener, not a bull flattener. (2) Risk assets sold off hard on 7/29: S&P -1.52% to 7,316, Dow -2.19% (-1,100pts), Nasdaq -1.74%, with the Nasdaq 100 entering correction. (3) The proximate equity story is AI-capex skepticism, not rates alone: Meta missed by $1.04 (EPS $6.18), expenses +55% to $42bn vs revenue +28%, net income -14%, and guided Q3 light — shares -6% to -10% after hours. Microsoft beat (rev $90.01bn vs $87.62bn est, Azure +43% cc) and rose ~2.4%. SK Hynix disappointed and semis were the worst group. (4) Geopolitics: Iran launched an attempted surprise attack, the first US-Iran re-engagement since the recent pause; Brent jumped over 7% through $90, a seven-month high. Energy and utilities were the only groups showing positive breadth. (5) Inflation is 3.5% headline / 2.6% core and cooling, but a $90+ oil impulse plus three hike dissents means the disinflation trade is over. (6) Gold sits at $4,066, far below the January $5,595 peak, and notably ROSE 0.94% on the hawkish day when yields rose — a resilience tell and cleaner positioning. (7) XLU has 90% of constituents above their 200-day EMA, the highest breadth of any of the 11 sectors, driven by AI power demand rather than by duration. (8) DXY is rangebound near 101, not breaking out, which weakens the dollar-strength half of my EFA-short case.

How this maps onto my measured seasonal windows: the macro regime AGREES with my highest-conviction stats (short IEF, long XLI, long XLF/KRE — a bear steepener is the single best backdrop for bank NIM, and industrials carry my strongest measured window at 81% hit rate and t=+2.49/+3.78) and FIGHTS my weakest stat (QQQ minus SPY was only t=+1.35, the least significant number in my entire study, and it now sits against a correction, an AI-capex de-rating and rising discount rates). Gold's Aug-Sep restocking window is reinforced by a live shooting war and an oil-driven inflation impulse. Utilities' rate sensitivity is offset by best-in-market breadth and a structural power-demand bid.

Decision history — 6 recorded events
  1. 2026-07-27OPENEDOpening book registered · experiments/round3/allocations/opus5_seasonality.json

    Outlook at registrationBase case is a mid-single-digit gain to year-end with materially smaller drawdowns than the index: the measured composite averaged +3.87% over Jul-27-to-Dec-31 in 17 of 20 past years with a worst case of -19.25% against SPY's -27.08%, so I expect to track near SPY with less pain rather than to beat it outright, and to lag if the tape runs hot. Management is calendar-scheduled rather than discretionary, using the weekly Friday reassessments. Around Sep-30 I intend to deploy the 7% cash into a BTC leg for the measured Uptober window (9/11 years, avg +19.4%, t=+3.60) with a stop, and to add to XLU, whose Sep-30-to-Oct-31 window is 19/26 years positive. Around Oct-31 I rotate the QQQ overweight toward mid/small caps for the Nov-Dec leg, where MDY minus SPY is +1.18% at t=+2.27 and IWM minus SPY is +1.42% at t=+1.67 while QQQ minus SPY is actually negative (10/26 years), and I add XRT for the holiday build (+3.80% avg, 13/20 years, and 7/10 in the last decade at +7.38%). I cover the IEF short if the Nov-Dec equity-over-duration spread has already paid, and I will cover EFA early if it outperforms SPY by more than 3% over any four-week stretch, since that is the direct falsifier of the leg. Within each month I bias any incremental buying to the turn-of-the-month window (last trading day through the third trading day, +0.263% average, 57% hit over 318 months) rather than mid-month. The risk I am carrying knowingly is that this is a screened-winner book with one observation per year per effect, so I will size down rather than double down if the Aug-Oct leg does not behave.

    Pre-registration backtest
    windows tested2026-01-02 to 2026-07-24; 2025-07-16 to 2025-12-31; 2025-07-28 to 2025-10-31; 2024-07-29 to 2024-10-31
    strategy return pct2026H1 +6.81%; 2025H2 +7.36%; 2025_seasonal_AugOct +4.67%; 2024_seasonal_AugOct +6.37%
    benchmark return pct2026H1_SPY +8.74%; 2025H2_SPY +9.87%; 2025_seasonal_AugOct_SPY +7.38%; 2024_seasonal_AugOct_SPY +4.7%
    max drawdown pct2026H1 -7.21%; 2025H2 -3.39%; 2025_seasonal_AugOct -2.03%; 2024_seasonal_AugOct -4.1%

    MULTIPLE TESTING IS THE MAIN CAVEAT AND I AM REPORTING SCREENED WINNERS. I screened 36 instruments across 5 calendar windows on an absolute basis, the same 36 relative to SPY, 24 explicit long/short spreads across 3 windows, plus turn-of-the-month and crypto calendar variants — well over 400 statistics. At 400 tests one expects several 70%+ hit rates by chance alone, and none of the reported t-statistics would survive a Bonferroni correction. That is why every position is quoted with its hit-rate and n rather than an average alone, and why I preferred effects that hold on BOTH the full sample and the last 10 years and have an economic flow story, over the higher-average but lower-hit-rate tail-driven ones (OIH -4.6% avg but only 36% hit; USO -9.9% avg but heavily contaminated by futures roll decay rather than seasonality). SAMPLE SIZE: the longest series give n=26 non-overlapping years, several (KRE, IEF, GLD) give only n=20-23, and the crypto statistic is n=11; a 21/26 hit rate has a one-sided binomial p of about 0.005 but is one observation per year, so the effective sample is tiny. WINDOW OVERLAP: Jul27-Sep30, Jul27-Oct31 and Jul27-Dec31 are nested, so their statistics are not independent evidence. HONEST NEGATIVE FINDINGS: (1) the famous 'August/September weakness' is NOT a directional edge — SPY was positive in 14/26 Aug-31-to-Sep-30 windows with a median of +0.30%; the negative -1.20% average is produced entirely by tail years (2001, 2002, 2008, 2022), so the correct trade is lower drawdown, not a short. (2) The seasonal window ahead is net POSITIVE (SPY Jul-27 to Dec-31 avg +3.90%, 19/26 years, t=+2.09), which is why this book is net long ~75% rather than market-neutral. (3) The book's measured edge is a higher hit rate (17/20 positive years vs SPY 19/26) and roughly 70% of SPY's drawdown, NOT reliable outperformance: it beat SPY in only 7/20 Jul-Dec windows and 11/20 Aug-Oct windows, and it lagged SPY in 3 of the 4 engine backtests above. In a strong bull tape this construction will underperform, and the recorded backtests show exactly that. ENGINE-SPECIFIC: shorts consume weight budget in this engine, so net exposure is capped at long-minus-short; the KRE stop is set at -25% and did not trigger in any of the four windows; an earlier candidate that shorted OIH was stopped out in both mandatory windows and was discarded, and an earlier candidate holding 4-5% BTC at entry underperformed this one in 3 of 4 windows, consistent with the measured BTC Aug-Sep statistic. All backtest figures above are verbatim from tracker/round2.py --backtest.

  2. 2026-07-31REBALANCEUnrestricted-retail resize (position caps lifted, free-internet research poll) · experiments/desk/unrestricted_resize_2026-07-30.json
    Stated reason (desk log)

    The regime changed under the book three days after I set it, and it changed in a way that sorts my legs cleanly by measured conviction rather than forcing me off mandate. I am not abandoning calendar seasonality — I am re-sizing it so that weight concentrates where my Jul-27-to-year-end statistics and the new macro point the same direction, and drains from where they conflict.

    CUT QQQ 20 -> 6. This was my largest position and my weakest evidence: QQQ minus SPY measured t=+1.35, the least significant statistic in my entire study, and I was carrying it at top weight purely because it was the 'growth core'. It now faces three simultaneous headwinds — the Nasdaq 100 is in correction, Meta missed by $1.04 with expenses +55% against revenue +28% and guided Q3 light, and rising long yields compress exactly this duration. I keep a 6% stub because QQQ's ABSOLUTE Jul-27 to Dec-31 window is still +3.97% at 20/26 years (77%) and Microsoft's Azure +43% shows the capex is at least buying revenue; it is the relative-to-SPY case, not the absolute case, that was thin. Sizing by measured conviction is the mandate, and this leg measured worst.

    SIZE UP IEF SHORT 4 -> 17. This is now the single cleanest idea I own. My seasonal read was already the most extreme number in the study — intermediate Treasuries beat SPY in only 5/23 years (22%) over this window and in just 1 of the last 10, at -6.00% average. The macro has now arrived at the same conclusion from the other side: three FOMC dissents for a hike, ~60-79% odds of a hike by September, a $90 Brent inflation impulse, and long yields that ROSE on a hold. At 4% this leg could not earn anything even if it was perfectly right. At 17% it can. 3% borrow over five months costs ~0.2% of NAV, which is cheap for the only leg that pays off in the scenario that hurts everything else I own.

    SIZE UP XLI 18 -> 20 and XLF 13 -> 16, KRE 6 -> 7. These carry my best measured windows (XLI +5.39%, 21/26 years, t=+2.49, with Nov-Dec at t=+3.78 and t=+3.04 versus SPY; XLF +5.04% at 20/26 and 9/10 in the last decade at +8.94%; KRE the highest-return sleeve at +7.24%, t=+2.28, 8/10 last decade at +10.14%). Crucially the macro now reinforces rather than merely permits them: a bear steepener with the Fed on hold and long yields rising is the textbook environment for bank net interest margin, and industrials are the cyclical least exposed to the AI-capex de-rating while benefiting from defense spending in an active Middle East conflict. Financials and industrials were both named in the broad-participation breadth data.

    SIZE UP GLD 13 -> 15. My cleanest non-equity seasonal (+3.54% Jul-27 to Oct-27, t=+1.69, +3.13% versus SPY at t=+1.80) now has a live geopolitical and inflation catalyst stacked on top, and the tell that matters is that gold rose 0.94% on the hawkish day while yields rose. Positioning is also far cleaner at $4,066 than at the January $5,595 peak. This is simultaneously my seasonal leg and the hedge that pays if the September hike breaks my cyclical longs.

    HOLD XLU 9 -> 8. I expected to cut this as a bond proxy into a hiking scare, but the breadth data argued me out of it: 90% of XLU constituents sit above their 200-day EMA, the strongest of all 11 sectors, because the bid is AI power demand rather than duration. Combined with a positive measured Sep-30 to Oct-31 window (19/26 years, 8/10 in the last decade) I keep it near full size, trimming a point for rate risk.

    DROP XLP 5 -> 0. Painful because it had my highest t-statistic (t=+3.32 absolute, t=+3.93 for Nov-Dec), but that edge is concentrated in the Oct-31 to Dec-31 leg, and staples face input-cost compression from a $90 oil shock in the meantime. This is a timing decision, not a rejection: I intend to re-enter it with cash at the November rotation, which is exactly what the dry powder is for.

    TRIM EFA SHORT 5 -> 5 (unchanged). I nearly cut this. The seasonal case is genuinely good (positive in only 9/24 years, 2/10 in the last decade at -2.65%), but half of its mechanism was dollar strength and DXY is stuck near 101 rather than breaking out — and a US-led tech correction can actually flatter less tech-heavy foreign indices. Holding at existing size rather than adding, since its natural pair (long QQQ) just shrank by two thirds.

    CASH 7 -> 6. I release one point to fund the IEF short while preserving essentially all pre-committed dry powder for the Oct-1 and Nov-1 rotations, when XLP and the mid/small-cap shift come back on.

    Standing orders: I tighten KRE's stop from -25% to -20%, because the original -25% was calibrated to the 2008 drawdown as a pure beta event, whereas the live risk is credit stress from a hike landing on top of an oil shock, which would show up faster. I add a -18% stop on the QQQ stub and a -12% stop on EFA. I attach a -10% stop to the IEF short: if intermediate Treasuries rally 10% against me that is a flight-to-quality recession event, in which case my industrials, financials and regional banks are all bleeding too and I want that leg closed rather than doubling the correlation. I put a +30% take-profit on GLD to bank an extreme war spike, set deliberately wide so it does not decapitate the hedge during ordinary strength. Taking the next available fill rather than naming a date — I am adding to cyclicals into a flush, which is the right side of this print, and waiting for a bounce to sell my QQQ cut would be over-cleverness.

  3. 2026-08-10REBALANCERegistered rebalance · experiments/round3/weeks/2026-08-10/opus5_seasonality.json
    Registered book note — experiments/round3/weeks/2026-08-10/opus5_seasonality.json

    Weekly desk 2026-08-08: Last week I re-sized this book on a hawkish macro overlay and the overlay inverted within five sessions, so I am unwinding the overlay rather than the mandate. The 17% IEF short and the 6% QQQ stub were both sized on a September hike I no longer have evidence for: payrolls printed -23k against +83k expected with 103k of downward revisions and participation at a five-year low, hike odds fell from roughly 60-79% to 35-46%, the 10Y fell to 4.6%, and the AI-capex de-rating that justified gutting QQQ was refuted by AWS +37% and Azure +43% while the Nasdaq ran +5.2%. My measured Jul-27-to-year-end statistics never moved — what moved was the macro I had layered on top of them, and every leg I now change is one where the macro was doing the sizing rather than the study. Concretely: IEF short 17->6 returns it to the size its seasonal statistic alone supports, because a bond short is the single worst place to be if the labor market is genuinely rolling; QQQ 6->17 restores the large-cap-growth sleeve my mandate explicitly names, on the absolute window (+3.97%, 77%) that was always the sound half of that case, with falling yields now helping the duration that was hurting it; GLD 15->18 because the driver rotated from war premium to falling real rates, which is the cleaner and more persistent version of the same trade and lands squarely inside my measured Jul-27-to-Oct-27 window; EFA short 5->3 because a falling dollar on US labor weakness disables half the mechanism, leaving only the seasonal relative stat to carry it; and XLI 20->16 because it is my best statistic but has slid from 3rd to 6th in sector rank with deteriorating relative strength and is the cyclical most exposed if payrolls were a signal rather than noise. XLF up a point on a confirmed breakout and positive rotation, XLU up a point because lower yields help it during exactly its measured Aug-Sep leg, KRE flat with a tighter stop because the seasonal is my highest-return sleeve but a weakening labor market is precisely how regional-bank credit costs stop being manageable. Cash back to the 7% the mandate pre-commits for the Oct-1 and Nov-1 rotations.

  4. 2026-08-17REBALANCERegistered rebalance · experiments/round3/weeks/2026-08-17/opus5_seasonality.json
    Registered book note — experiments/round3/weeks/2026-08-17/opus5_seasonality.json

    Weekly desk 2026-08-15: Last week I wrote that my error was re-sizing this book on a macro overlay that then inverted inside five sessions. That overlay has now inverted a second time — Hormuz talks stalled, the blockade may run indefinitely, unprecedented Iran sanctions land next week, Brent +5% to $87, and the 30Y rose 6bp even as retail sales missed by 70bp. If I chased that back into the book I would be committing the identical error in the opposite direction, so I am deliberately not touching the macro-sensitive legs: IEF stays at its seasonal 6% and QQQ stays at 17%. I am making exactly one substantive trade, and it is driven by a fact about a specific sleeve rather than by a macro regime call. The Russell 2000 printed a record high this week WITHOUT regional banks — KRE remains below its 2022 peak while AI-linked small caps carried the index — and that stall arrived in the same week retail sales fell 0.6% and UMich sentiment hit 51, which is the consumer-credit input that hits spread lenders hardest and the very risk I flagged when I declined to add KRE last week. My own conclusion then was that the incremental dollar of financials exposure belongs in XLF, and this week's tape made that argument for me: XLF is ranked 3rd, its breakout above the prior high is holding, its RRG lines point up, and a steepening curve with the long end pinned by oil-driven inflation premium is precisely its setup. So I move 2 points from the high-beta expression to the confirmed one, staying inside the same mandate sleeve rather than changing my sector allocation. Second, I am harvesting the gold windfall through the exit rather than the notional: GLD has earned roughly 2.5x its entire measured Jul-27-to-Oct-27 window average in the first third of that window, which by my own calendar logic is exhaustion, but selling the week before an announced escalation is fighting a dated catalyst — so I hold 18% and cut the take-profit from +25% to +18%, which sits near $4,800 and converts an unrealized seasonal win into a committed one before the window closes. Everything else holds because nothing sleeve-specific changed: XLI keeps its 16% through the soft patch because the statistical mass is the Nov-Dec leg at t=+3.78 and one weak consumer month is not a reason to abandon it, XLU stays at 9% because my own numbers say it is relative-negative to SPY until Sep-30 and the add belongs to the Oct-1 rotation, and the 7% cash stays untouched as the pre-committed Oct-1 and Nov-1 dry powder my mandate specifies — which is also where the KRE weight goes back on, into its actual Oct-31-to-Dec-31 window.

    Registered book note — experiments/round3/weeks/2026-08-24/opus5_seasonality.json

    Weekly desk 2026-08-22: One funding decision, not a rebuild: utilities is the single leg where my own measured calendar and the tape now agree that I am early, and I am moving that capital into the two legs where the same force is doing the work. XLU Jul-27-to-Sep-30 is +1.14% absolute but MINUS 0.55% versus SPY in my study — the sleeve only earns Sep-30 to Oct-31 (+1.24%, 19/26 years) — and this week the tape stopped disagreeing politely and ranked it dead last, 11th of 11, down from 7th, for the mechanical reason that a bond proxy yielding 2.5-3% cannot compete with a 19-year-high 30Y at 5.28%. I cut it to 4% and the add still belongs to my earmarked Oct-1 rotation cash. The proceeds go where confirmation arrived: XLI, the strongest statistic in my entire window set (+5.39%, 81%, t=+2.49, Nov-Dec leg t=+3.78), jumped from 6th of eleven to 3rd, broke a multi-month consolidation and is nearing RRG leadership — last week I held it through weakness on the number alone, so I add now that the tape has come to the number. XLF goes to 20% because it holds its breakout at rank 2 with a 19% model weight while the curve steepens into its net interest margin. IEF short goes 6% to 8% — a deliberate half-step, not the 17% I once carried — because the long-end selloff has finally separated itself from the September-hike bet that inverted on me twice: that bet is dead and the 30Y still made a 19-year high on deficit supply, AI-corporate issuance and Warsh saying he will not hike against inflation. That is a term-premium mechanism with a much longer half-life, and it is the same mechanism paying XLF and punishing XLU. I stop short of a bigger add only because Warsh's first Jackson Hole is next week and a dovish belly rally is a real two-sided risk. I do not touch QQQ, GLD, KRE or EFA: changing QQQ would be my third directional flip on that sleeve in six weeks over a semis rotation my own study says reverses into Nov-Dec, and selling GLD 2.5% below a pre-set take-profit into a live catalyst stack is exactly the bad execution I refused last week.

  6. 2026-08-31REBALANCERegistered rebalance · experiments/round3/weeks/2026-08-31/opus5_seasonality.json
    Registered book note — experiments/round3/weeks/2026-08-31/opus5_seasonality.json

    Weekly desk 2026-08-29: One mechanism in this book reversed this week and I am repricing only the legs that were actually bought off it, not rebuilding. For three weeks every leg here has leaned on the same claim I wrote down explicitly: Warsh will not hike against inflation, so the long end rises on deficit supply and term premium while the short end stays anchored — a bear steepener. On Friday he said the opposite, September hike odds went from ~30% to 50-60% in a day, the 2Y jumped 6bps to 4.298% and the long end edged LOWER. That is a bear flattener. I am not entitled to keep the positions I sized off a forecast that just inverted. Gold takes the largest cut because I am the one who wrote last week that its bid was a 'debasement and Fed-credibility bid' from that exact mechanism — with credibility being restored by a hiking chair, that reason is gone, and separately my own calendar says the Jul-27-to-Oct-27 window (+3.54% average) is roughly 4x spent at ~+12.5%. I do not need price to reach my $4,798 exit to admit the reason I was holding has expired. XLF gives back precisely the increment I added for the steepener and keeps the core the calendar justifies. KRE goes to a token because the specific engine of 2026 regional NIM expansion is deposit costs rolling over, and a hike re-inflates them at the exact institutions with no fee-income cushion. Against that, two legs got confirming evidence: NVDA's beat-and-raise and an 8.7% session is the cleanest available refutation of the AI-capex-and-financing bear case I named as QQQ's risk last week, in a week where only 3 of 11 sectors rose and leadership narrowed back into my sleeve; and on IEF I stated the precise condition for adding — that I would not size into a dated catalyst I could not handicap — which has now passed and resolved in my favour, with the belly the part of the curve a hiking cycle bites hardest. XLI and XLU stay untouched because nothing changed for them and a one-point nudge is churn, not a decision. Cash rises 7% to 14% as pre-committed dry powder for the Oct-1 utilities rotation and the Nov-1 regional/financials rotation, which is where the overwhelming mass of my measured window return actually sits, earning 4% through the one month of my window that measures negative.

Research notes — free-internet poll, desk run 2026-07-30

Searched the tape for 27-30 Jul 2026 plus each sleeve in my book. Key findings: (1) REGIME SHOCK 29 Jul — Fed (Chair Warsh) held rates at 3.50-3.75% but THREE FOMC members dissented in favour of a HIKE; long-dated yields jumped, Dow -1,100 (-2.2%), S&P -1.5%, Nasdaq -1.7% with the semis/AI selloff deepening after SK Hynix. Markets are now pricing hikes, not cuts (June headline PCE 3.6%, core 3.3%, CPI 4.2%). (2) ENERGY IS THE DOMINANT TREND — Iran has blocked the Strait of Hormuz since late Feb; Iran rejected Oman's 50-50 control proposal; Brent surged >7% to $90+ and WTI to ~$83 on 29 Jul after a three-day diplomacy-driven dip to $79. Energy prices +20% in two weeks is what turned the Fed hawkish. (3) DOLLAR — Fed/ECB rate gap is the dominant FX driver; hawkish Fed vs softer eurozone inflation; consensus EUR/USD 1.12 for Q3 vs ~1.14 spot; DXY basing near 100.6 off a 101.4 high. Confirms the EUO leg. (4) PRECIOUS METALS DOWNTREND INTACT AND RE-FUELLED — gold ~$4,140, -26% from Jan's $5,598 record; silver ~$58-60, -52% from Jan's $121.62; OCBC sees further declines on rising Treasury yields and a stronger dollar. Rising real yields is exactly the 29 Jul catalyst. (5) HEALTHCARE LEADS — XLV was the top S&P sector on 28 Jul (+2.33%, with staples +1.96%); pharma-led, defensive leadership is what you expect in a hawkish/risk-off tape. (6) SMALL CAPS ARE THE BROKEN LEG — R2K +17-18% YTD but BofA estimates every extra 25bp hike cuts R2K operating earnings ~2%; hike-dissent Fed, floating-rate debt and refi needs make small caps the single most rate-hike-exposed sleeve, and my own screen already had IWM only 0.1% above its 50dma. (7) URA -18% over the past month and -10% over the past week even with spot uranium firm at $85-86.60 — the miners/equity complex is de-rating independently of the commodity; sharpest active downtrend in my universe. (8) BTC ~$63.9k, stabilising after a 21-month low near $58k, total crypto cap -48% from peak, driven by the Fed and ETF outflows — downtrend intact but a bounce is in progress. (9) XLF made a record high $56.18 (+8.7% in three months) — trend intact, but it is the highest equity-beta and credit-cycle-sensitive long I own into a hiking Fed.

StrategySystematic time-series trend across six asset classes: every candidate is scored on price vs its 50- and 200-day moving average plus 3-month time-series momentum computed from data through the 2026-07-24 close, long where both filters are positive and short where both are negative, sized inversely to 60-day realised volatility so each sleeve contributes similar risk, with wide catastrophe stops rather than tight exits because the engine's stops are fixed-from-entry and weekly reassessment is the real trend-exit mechanism.

  1. 2026-07-27OPENEDOpening book registered · experiments/round3/allocations/opus5_trend.json

    Outlook at registrationExpect a low-beta, low-drawdown return stream that looks nothing like the index: net equity exposure is only about +38% gross long minus 8% short, and roughly half the risk budget sits in currency (EUO), agriculture (DBA), energy (XLE/USO) and the short metals/crypto sleeve. In a continuation regime the dollar, financials, healthcare and energy legs compound while the metals and crypto shorts pay a second time; in a chop regime both sides bleed at once and the wide stops mean the book gives back slowly rather than crashing. Management plan: re-sign every market at each Friday reassessment on the same two filters (price vs 200dma AND 3-month time-series momentum), flip or flatten any leg whose filters disagree, re-scale weights to 60-day inverse vol, and cut the whole book toward cash if fewer than half the universe shows a coherent trend. The specific things I will watch are gold reclaiming its 50dma (would flatten GLD/SLV), BTC closing back above its 200dma (would cover the perp), and XLK/SOXL basing - if tech re-accelerates while XLY stays weak the short-discretionary leg becomes the wrong hedge.

    Pre-registration backtest
    windows tested2026-01-02 to 2026-07-24; 2025-07-16 to 2025-12-31; 2025-01-02 to 2025-06-30
    strategy return pct2026H1 +12.55%; 2025H2 +1.83%; 2025H1 -6.14%
    benchmark return pct2026H1_SPY +8.74%; 2025H2_SPY +9.87%; 2025H1_SPY +6.31%
    max drawdown pct2026H1 -3.25%; 2025H2 -3.93%; 2025H1 -9.42%

    Run through tracker/round2.py --backtest on this exact file; numbers verbatim. THE STATIC-BOOK LIMITATION IS THE HEADLINE CAVEAT: a real managed-futures program re-signs every market every week and would have been LONG gold, silver, uranium and crypto through most of 2025, whereas this book is frozen short them because that is what the 2026-07-24 signal says. The two 2025 windows therefore do not test the strategy, they test what happens when a trend book is forced to hold last-quarter's signal through the prior trend - which is why 2025H1 is -6.14% (EUO and IWM stopped out in the spring dollar/small-cap reversal, the short-metals sleeve fought a bull market) and 2025H2 is +1.83% with all four metals/crypto shorts stopped or taken out. The 2026H1 window is the only one where the entry signals resembled the current ones, and there the book returned +12.55% against SPY +8.74% with a -3.25% drawdown, i.e. it beat the index at roughly a third of its volatility. Read the 2025 windows as a downside stress test of signal staleness rather than as strategy performance. Second caveat: the engine's stop_loss_pct is fixed-from-entry, not trailing, so tight stops whipsaw - an earlier variant with 12-18% stops cut XLF at its April low in 2026H1 and returned only +7.57%; widening to 18-45% catastrophe stops and relying on the weekly reassessment for trend exits added ~5pp. Third: entry costs and 3% borrow are charged by the engine, but the backtest legs have prev_alloc=None so no rebalance turnover cost is modelled, and daily-close granularity means the BTC perp could survive an intraday liquidation.

  2. 2026-07-31REBALANCEUnrestricted-retail resize (position caps lifted, free-internet research poll) · experiments/desk/unrestricted_resize_2026-07-30.json
    Stated reason (desk log)

    The trend signals I built this book on were not just confirmed this week, they were re-fuelled by a genuine regime event on 29 Jul: a hawkish Fed hold with three dissents FOR A HIKE, long yields up, Brent +7% to $90+ on Hormuz. That single catalyst simultaneously strengthens my dollar long (widening Fed/ECB gap), my precious-metals shorts (rising real yields is THE gold driver, and OCBC/consensus now sees further declines), my energy long (Hormuz supply constraint is what turned the Fed hawkish in the first place), my defensive healthcare long (XLV was the top S&P sector on 28 Jul at +2.33% while the index fell 1.5%), and my consumer-discretionary short (4.2% CPI plus an energy shock plus hike risk is a direct squeeze on discretionary spend). So this is not a rebuild, it is a conviction-weighted resize of the same eleven trends, which is exactly what the new sizing freedom is for. Three changes. FIRST, I EXIT IWM ENTIRELY. It was already my weakest signal (only 0.1% above its 50dma, i.e. the fast trend had gone flat while the slow one was still up), and the 29 Jul event is precisely the catalyst that breaks it: BofA puts the damage at ~2% of R2K operating earnings per 25bp, small caps carry the most floating-rate debt and refi need, and a hike-biased Fed favours large balance sheets. Weekly reassessment is my real trend-exit mechanism and this is what it is for - I do not wait for a -20% catastrophe stop to tell me a trend has rolled. SECOND, I lift the four legs where the macro driver and the price trend now point the same way and the volatility is low enough to justify size: EUO 14 to 19 (lowest vol in the book at 9.9%, cleanest macro trend, inverse-vol sizing makes it the top weight on merit not on hunch), XLE 9 to 15 (best-established MA trend among the low-vol-enough names, 15.5% above its 200dma, with a live and re-accelerating supply catalyst), GLD short 6 to 10 and XLY short 8 to 10. XLV goes 13 to 14 and URA short 2 to 3 - URA is down 18% in a month and 10% in a week even with spot uranium firm at $86, the sharpest active downtrend I can find, capped only by its 51.8% vol. THIRD, I trim XLF 16 to 10. The trend is genuinely intact (record high $56.18, +8.7% in three months) so I am not exiting, but it is my highest equity-beta and most credit-cycle-exposed long and a hiking Fed is not its friend; that capital works harder in the dollar and energy legs. USO goes 3 to 5 but no further - 38% above its 200dma against 3m momentum of only +1.5% is the definition of an extended trend where the two filters disagree, and 51.7% vol plus whipsaw risk on any Hormuz diplomacy headline (oil fell three straight days to $79 before the 29 Jul spike) keeps it small with a -40% stop. I am NOT going to a one-line book. My mandate is time-series trend across six asset classes sized inversely to realised volatility, and the whole edge is that the equity, FX, commodity, metals and crypto sleeves each contribute similar risk from independent drivers - collapsing that into one name would be abandoning the strategy, not expressing conviction in it. Gross equity 94% keeps me inside the no-margin cap, cash 3% earns 4%, and the turnover here is a handful of basis points on maybe 30% of the book.
